headlines.title: 제조업 부진에 … 26년5개월만에 상용직 줄었다

key_headlines.title: South Korea's May exports hit record 87.8 billion dollars, driven by semiconductor boom
key_headlines.summary: Korea's monthly exports reached an all-time high of 87.8 billion dollars in May, with semiconductor exports surging 167.7% year-over-year, maintaining 12 consecutive months of export growth.

key_headlines.title: US-Iran ceasefire agreement lifts global markets; KOSPI jumps 5% at open
key_headlines.summary: Following the US-Iran peace accord announcement, KOSPI index surged 5% at market open, WTI crude fell to the 80 dollar range, and the won strengthened as geopolitical tensions eased.

key_headlines.title: Bank of Japan expected to raise rates from 0.75% to 1.0% on June 16
key_headlines.summary: The Bank of Japan is anticipated to increase its policy rate by 25 basis points to 1.0% following multiple rate-hike signals, with the decision to be announced on June 16.

key_headlines.title: K-shaped polarization in Korean economy worsens in Q2 with semiconductors dominating profits
key_headlines.summary: Semiconductor companies alone posted 961% operating profit growth, with Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, and Hanmi contributing 84% of top 30 companies' 175 trillion won earnings, while 27 non-semiconductor firms face declining profits.

key_headlines.title: Kevin Warsh to chair first FOMC meeting as new Fed chair on June 17
key_headlines.summary: The Federal Reserve's FOMC meeting on June 17 marks the first monetary policy decision under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, with markets focused on forward interest rate guidance.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economy showed strong momentum in May with record exports of 87.8 billion dollars, marking the third consecutive month above 80 billion dollars, primarily driven by exceptional semiconductor performance with 167.7% year-over-year growth. The trade surplus reached 27 billion dollars for the 16th consecutive month, with imports rising 20.7% to 60.8 billion dollars. However, Korea's economy is experiencing sharp K-shaped divergence, with semiconductor companies posting 961% operating profit increases while non-semiconductor firms face declining earnings, highlighting growing inequality among major conglomerates.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Import prices fell 0.3% month-over-month for the second consecutive month following the US-Iran ceasefire agreement, easing inflationary pressures from previous geopolitical tensions and high oil prices. Export prices rose 0.3% month-over-month due to sustained semiconductor price increases from AI-driven demand, marking 11 consecutive months of export price growth. Despite falling international crude oil prices, inflation concerns persist as import prices remain elevated compared to year-ago levels, though the won-to-dollar exchange rate has begun strengthening from prior highs, supporting price stability expectations going forward.
sections.Financial Markets: KOSPI index surged 5% at market open following the US-Iran ceasefire announcement, with the won-dollar exchange rate rebounding from 1,503.9 won toward the 1,400 won level as geopolitical risk premiums evaporated. Foreign investors, however, conducted massive profit-taking with net sales of 70.2 billion dollars in May stocks and 5.6 billion dollar net inflows in bonds, resulting in net capital outflows of approximately 39 trillion won from Korean financial markets. Markets are now focused on the June 17 FOMC meeting under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh to gauge the Federal Reserve's monetary policy trajectory, with expectations for potential KOSPI advancement toward the 9,000 level if positive signals emerge.
sections.Industry & Technology: The US-Iran ceasefire has provided relief to Korea's semiconductor industry by reducing geopolitical uncertainties and stabilizing supply chains, while battery and electric vehicle sectors face a challenging test amid softening EV demand. KOSDAQ's 30-year identity is shifting from biotech to semiconductor, as AI investment expansion increases demand for high-bandwidth memory production-related companies in packaging, testing, and equipment sectors. Automotive stocks have benefited from robot-related developments, prompting reassessment of valuations across hybrid, electric, autonomous, and hydrogen vehicle segments. Iron Device has been selected for government-backed R&D projects focused on gallium nitride (GaN) power modules for electric vehicles.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's jeonse (long-term lease) and monthly rental markets are facing severe shortages, with combined prices surging as new apartment supply drops to 27,158 units this year from 37,103 units last year, a 26.9% decline. Despite rising apartment prices in Pyeongtaek, subscription applications remain weak, with 3,389 unoccupied units recorded in April, indicating market disconnect between prices and buyer demand. Major reconstruction projects are progressing with the 'Wolgyae Mimi-Sam' complex transforming into a 6,000-unit mega-development, and Samsung E&C selected as the constructor for the 653.8 billion won 'Bangbae Shin-Samho' reconstruction project after lengthy delays.
sections.International Economy: The Dow Jones Index reached an all-time high and the Nasdaq surged 3.1% following the US-Iran ceasefire announcement, with international crude oil prices falling 5% to three-month lows as geopolitical risk dissipated. European indices including Eurostoxx 600 also rose as AI-related semiconductor stocks led gains globally, while the US dollar weakened and won-dollar rates improved. Markets are now intensely focused on the June 17 FOMC meeting under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh to determine future interest rate policy direction, with this being his first monetary policy decision as central bank chief.
sections.AI & Economy: Chinese large language models like DeepSeek are rapidly gaining market share in AI model markets by emphasizing cost-effectiveness over raw performance, with weekly usage volumes surpassing US frontier models for general tasks and emerging AI agent applications. DeepSeek's token usage ranked first among alternatives due to its open-architecture aggressive supply strategy, while performance gaps may lead to hybrid usage patterns where high-importance tasks use US models and routine work employs Chinese alternatives. The South Korean government and Samsung Electronics have joined forces on a national AI chip development project to strengthen Korea's fabless semiconductor competitiveness amid the AI boom. Sision AI is projected to achieve profitability this year through expanded AI solution revenue and robot automation business growth, leveraging its vision AI technology in airport, corporate, and government facility applications.
sections.Others: The Hormuz Strait is expected to reopen following the US-Iran peace accord MOU, though disputes remain over toll collection rights between the US and Iran regarding this critical waterway handling approximately 20% of global crude oil flows. China's advanced manufacturing sectors are rapidly embracing AI and robot technologies for automation, though this transformation intensifies structural youth unemployment challenges in the Chinese economy as jobs become automated. The Korea Power Exchange has completed power grid control dualization by opening its Chungbuk Osong headquarters, establishing disaster-resilient power management systems. Space industry investment interest is rising with SpaceX's anticipated IPO, prompting firms like Kiwoom Asset Management to launch space-themed ETFs with up to 25% SpaceX exposure.
